title: Reverse the 2026 farm and family-business inheritance tax changes
headline: Undo the 2026 farm and family-business relief cuts. Costs £0.5bn.
description: Autumn Budget 2024 cut agricultural property relief and business property relief from April 2026: 100% relief on the first £1 million of combined assets and 50% above it, with 50% relief for unlisted shares on recognised exchanges. Switch this on to restore full relief from April 2027, giving up the Treasury's costing of the reform (£495m in 2027-28 and £520m a year after, carried to 2030-31 with the OBR's inheritance tax forecast).

baselinePolicy.text: Agricultural and business property relief reformed from 6 April 2026: 100% relief for the first £1m of combined assets and 50% thereafter, and 50% relief for unlisted shares (Autumn Budget 2024, Table 5.1 line 29).

lines.title: Inheritance Tax: Reform agricultural property relief and business property relief from 6 April 2026 by maintaining 100% relief for the first £1m of combined assets and 50% relief thereafter, and 50% relief for “not listed” shares on the markets of a recognised stock exchange

rawSource.note: Reversal: the Treasury's costing with its sign reversed for 2027-28 to 2029-30; 2030-31 carries the 2029-30 figure forward with the OBR's inheritance tax receipts path.

uprating.head: receiptsByTax.inheritanceTax
uprating.note: Applied in the years the scorecard covers and extended to 2030-31 with the OBR's inheritance tax receipts (ADR-0004).

caveats: The Treasury's line bundles agricultural relief, business relief and the change for unlisted shares; the parts cannot be separated from published figures. The costing is on the OBR's October 2024 forecast; the level is not rebased.

The OBR's inheritance tax line more than doubles over the forecast as pensions come into estates from 2027; carrying the 2029-30 figure with that line for 2030-31 may overstate a relief that has nothing to do with pensions.

considerations.text: The Treasury's scorecard figure is the certified costing of the October 2024 reform, including the behavioural response the Treasury and OBR agreed at the time: more lifetime giving and restructuring of estates.

The OBR's inheritance tax forecast has been revised repeatedly as the reliefs, thresholds and the treatment of pensions changed; receipts are forecast to rise from £8.7bn in 2025-26 to £14.7bn in 2030-31. A small relief's cost sits inside a line that is itself moving fast.

interactions.text: Both change inheritance tax: the reform's costing was at a 40% rate, so a different rate changes what restoring the reliefs costs.
Both move inheritance tax reliefs; each is costed on its own and the combination is approximate.
